The Lok Sabha has been reconvened from Monday, while the Rajya Sabha will resume its sitting  from Wednesday to transact essential government business. The sittings of both the Houses, subject to exigencies of the Business, may conclude on the 3rd of December. There would be no Question Hour, Zero Hour and Private Members’ Business during the sittings of both the Houses. The move follows a government’s proposal to convene special sitting of both Houses. A report:

 

 

         

”As per the Lok Sabha Bulletin, Speaker Om Birla has directed that Lok Sabha, which was adjourned sine-die on the 13th of August, 2026, will now sit at 11 AM on Monday. The Rajya Sabha Bulletin also stated that the Upper House, which was adjourned sine die on 13th of August, has been reconvened by the Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan to meet at 11 AM on Wednesday to transact essential government business. Earlier, the Government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the sittings of Lower House and Upper House on these dates to transact essential Government Business. The Monsoon Session has not been prorogued so far following the adjournment of both the Houses sine die on August 13. With Anand Kumar, SAUMYA SHARAN FOR AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

India will host the 25th Indian Ocean Rim Association, IORA  Council of Ministers Meeting in New Delhi today. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Seychelles Barry Faure, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mauritius Dhananjay Ramful, and Sri Lankan Foreign Affairs Minister Vijitha Herath will participate in the IORA Council of Ministers Meeting among others. The theme for India’s IORA chairship 2025-2027 is “Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region”. Our correspondent has filed this report:

 

 

”This high-level gathering of Ministers from across the 23 Member States and 12 Dialogue Partners comes at a critical juncture for the Indo-Pacific region. It is slated to deliberate on future policy direction for IORA with an emphasis on reviewing regional cooperation frameworks and identifying new areas of collaboration. The New Delhi Meeting will underscore the vital importance of the Indian Ocean Region as a region of peace, stability, predictability and sustainable development. It will reaffirm India’s commitment to the vision of MAHASAGAR  driving collective action for an open, inclusive, and rules-based maritime order. IORA is an intergovernmental organization established on 7th March, 1997, to promote regional cooperation and sustainable development around the Indian Ocean. SUPARNA SAIKIA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

President Droupadi Murmu will be on a two-day visit to Keralam beginning today. During the visit, she will attend various events in the state. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

         

”The President will arrive in Kochi today morning and proceed to Kalady in Ernakulam where the President will visit Adi Shankaracharya’s birthplace.

 

Thereafter, the President will proceed to Thrissur to grace the Valedictory Ceremony of the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College as the Chief Guest (at 12.30 pm).

 

In the afternoon, the President will proceed to Guruvayur and will have darshan at the Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple.

 

On the second day of the visit,that is on November 28, the President will grace the Passing Out Parade at the Indian Naval Academy, Ezhimala in Kannur, as the Chief Guest (8 am). More than 400 officer trainees from various courses, including cadets from friendly foreign countries, will participate in the Passing Out Parade. THIS IS SHAMILA AKASHVANI NEWS KOCHI.”

Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan reviewed security situation in Jammu and Kashmir, with focus on counter-terrorism measures, border infiltration, winter security arrangements and presence of foreign terrorists in the region. Yesterday’s meeting brought together top officials from the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, Intelligence Bureau, heads of Central Armed Police Forces, senior Army commanders, Jammu and Kashmir Police officers and representatives of various intelligence and security agencies. The participants examined the prevailing security challenges and reviewed ongoing operations against militants, particularly in the mountainous and forested belts of the Jammu division, where foreign terrorists are believed to be operating. The meeting also discussed possible infiltration attempts, the need for stronger intelligence-sharing mechanisms and improved coordination among security agencies to deal with emerging threats.

The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will conclude today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Organised annually by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, it is one of India’s leading multi-product trade exhibitions. The theme of the fair this year is Vikas aur Virasat. An Award Presentation Ceremony was held yesterday, recognising outstanding displays and presentations by participating states and exhibitors. In the States and Union Territories category, Tamil Nadu was honoured with the gold award, Kerala received the silver award, Madhya Pradesh bagged the bronze award while Tripura received the commendation prize. In the Ministries and Government Departments category, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) received the Gold Medal, the Ministry of Railways received the Silver Medal and the Ministry of Textiles received the Bronze Medal.

 

 

Talking to the media, ITPO Chairman Jawed Ashraf said that this year the fair witnessed a significant increase in footfall compared to last year. He also highlighted that exhibitors witnessed higher business this year compared to the previous edition.

The 57th International Film Festival of India in Goa enters its eighth day today, with a star-studded panel discussion, filmmaker interactions and an exciting line-up of films adding to the celebrations. With just two days remaining, the festival continues to bring together celebrated filmmakers, emerging talent and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. Today’s highlights include a special discussion featuring Farhan Akhtar, Ashutosh Gowariker and Madhur Bhandarkar, along with the screening of the much-awaited first episode of Panchayat Season Five. More from our correspondent:

 

 

         

From celebrating iconic films to exploring new cinematic possibilities, Day Eight of IFFI promises another exciting journey through the world of cinema.

         

 

The spotlight will be on The Legendary 25’s, a panel discussion featuring filmmaker and actor Farhan Akhtar, filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker and director Madhur Bhandarkar. The session will revisit the cinematic journey and legacy of three landmark films released in 2001, Dil Chahta Hai, Lagaan and Chandni Bar. Later in the afternoon, filmmaker Karthik Subbaraj will take part in an interactive session titled, ‘What if the Villain is Right?’, exploring unconventional perspectives in filmmaking.

         

Adding to the excitement for audiences, the first episode of Panchayat Season Five, directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra, will have a special screening at INOX Panjim. The festival will also feature a diverse selection of Indian and international films across its screening venues. While, open-air screenings will continue at Miramar Beach, Vagator Beach and Ravindra Bhavan in Margao, bringing the cinematic experience closer to the public.

         

As IFFI moves towards its grand finale tomorrow, Goa continues to celebrate the universal language of cinema under this year’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’.THIS IS VISHNU P S, FROM GOA.

India presented its “vision and proposed roadmap” for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission yesterday. The 30-minute presentation was followed by a brief discussion, with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission. The presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad’s preparedness, including sports infrastructure and the support extended by city, state, and central authorities to Indian Olympic Association(IOA). It also covered India’s experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games.

 

 

Germany, Hungary, Qatar, Republic of Korea, South Africa and Turkiye are the other countries who are bidding for the 2036 Games. After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an “anonymous survey” to get a sense of the general public’s view on India’s bid.

In Cricket, Sri Lanka A defeated India A by 8 wickets to reach the final of Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha last night. Chasing a target of 318 runs, Sri Lanka A scored 318 runs with the loss of 2 wickets in 41.3 overs, against India A in the first semi-final. Opting to bat first, India A scored 317 runs losing 8 wickets in stipulated 50 overs. For India A, Abhishek Sharma scored highest 78 runs off 63 balls. Sineth Jayawardena was declared player of the match. Sri Lanka A opener Sineth scored 105 off 70 balls.

         

 

Sri Lanka A will play Final on Sunday. The opponent will be decided today, when Pakistan A faces Bangladesh A in the 2nd Semi-Final at 3:30 PM IST in Doha.

The West Bengal government is taking a series of initiatives to make the upcoming Gangasagar Mela plastic-free, environment-friendly and compliant with international standards.

 

 

Modern tents will replace traditional hogla-leaf shelters for pilgrims. Several water ATMs will provide free drinking water, while paper cups and glasses will replace plastic ones. A special cultural stage will also host religious programmes.

 

 

Announcing this after a preparatory meeting at Nabanna yesterday, Chief Secretary Manoj Kumar Agarwal said special arrangements were being made to ensure cleanliness, improve bathing ghats and provide round-the-clock sanitation.

The Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) is being observed today to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on this day in 1949. Since 2015, the Constitution Day has been observed as an occasion to reflect upon the principles and values enshrined in the Constitution and renew the collective commitment to its ideals. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

 

 

 

“On the occasion, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs will facilitate an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. Various activities are being organised across the country by Ministries and Departments of the Government, State and Union Territories Governments, autonomous bodies and institutions to mark the occasion. The Ministry noted that various awareness and outreach activities are also being undertaken through digital platforms and community-based initiatives to promote understanding of the Constitution and its significance in the country’s democratic framework.

         

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

President Droupadi Murmu will address the occasion at Samvidhan Sadan in New Delhi. Dr Ambedkar Foundation, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, will organise the Constitution Day Celebration at Dr Ambedkar International Centre in New Delhi today. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar and Former Chief Justice of India Justice Uday Umesh Lalit will attend the programme. Mr Lalit will lead the reading of the Preamble and deliver the Constitution Day Lecture on the subject ‘Constitutional Governance and the Legacy of Dr B R Ambedkar’. AKSHIT VAIDYAN, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called upon citizens to uphold the spirit of the Constitution and work collectively towards building a developed India by 2047. In an op-ed in daily newspapers in English and Hindi the Prime Minister recalled the adoption of the Constitution in 1949 and urged to place India first in National endeavours. He noted that the Constitution must find resonance beyond Parliament and the courts and become an integral part of the collective consciousness of citizens, particularly the youth. He said the decision to observe 26 November as Constitution Day was aimed at deepening people’s connection with the Constitution. Paying tribute to Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and all members of the Constituent Assembly, Mr Modi said that their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution. Sharing his personal journey, the Prime Minister said the Constitution had made it possible for a person born into a family of modest means, with no privileges or advantages of birth, to shoulder the responsibility of serving the world’s largest democracy.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended greetings to all citizens on the occasion of the 77th anniversary of the Indian Constitution Day. In a social media post, the Prime Minister paid tribute to Dr BR Ambedkar and all the other great luminaries of the Constituent Assembly. He said that the gift they bestowed upon us in the form of the Constitution is an invaluable heritage of Indian democracy. Mr Modi said that it will continue to guide us in realizing the resolve for a developed India. He said that Constitution day is an occasion to reaffirm the commitment to strengthening the values enshrined in it.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of PRAGATI, a multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation yesterday. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed five critical infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors, with a total cost of over 78 thousand crore rupees. He said, timely execution of these projects must be accompanied by high standards of construction quality. Mr Modi also reviewed the Industrial Training Institute (ITI) ecosystem, including the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU). He called for close collaboration between States, ITIs and industry to translate these partnerships into better training and employment opportunities for young people. Mr Modi also called upon Public Sector Undertakings to assess their future manpower requirements and strengthen linkages with ITIs for training and recruitment in relevant trades.

The WAVES Film Bazaar at International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa attracted 2 thousand 288 delegates from 54 countries this year. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

 

 

“Two Letters of Intent for India-Chile co-productions have emerged as a major outcome of the 20th edition of the WAVES Film Bazaar, while 14 Memoranda of Understanding and agreements are nearing finalisation. Addressing a press conference in Goa yesterday, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat, said that WAVES Film Bazaar brought together 2 thousand 288 delegates from 54 countries, including 471 buyers.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

The festival also experienced a colourful IFFI Parade in Panaji, celebrating Goa’s cultural heritage through vibrant floats and folk performances. While the Aakash Kandil Competition added a creative spark to the celebrations, showcasing colourful lanterns inspired by IFFI’s Peacock mascot. The 6th day also witnessed acclaimed playback singer K. S. Chithra paying tributes to legendary singers Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki during a special session. Meanwhile, today, the seventh day promises an exciting line-up of events, including masterclasses by casting director Mukesh Chhabra on auditioning and actor selection, and Natalie Wade of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on the Academy Awards. Special screenings will include Rishab Shetty’s Kantara: A Legend Chapter 1, and the Marathi film Tu Aahes Na as a gala presentation. With Vishnu and Alex, this is Saira Mujtaba, fRom Goa.”

India has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at 61st International Art Exhibition of Venice Art Biennale 2026, marking a significant recognition of the country’s contemporary art and cultural heritage on the global stage. The award, announced by La Biennale di Venezia, was decided through public voting, with visitors selecting India’s National Pavilion as their favourite. The recognition comes as India returns to the prestigious international art exhibition after a gap of seven years. The India Pavilion attracted approximately 4.5 lakh visitors during the Biennale, placing it among the most visited national pavilions of the edition. The announcement of the Visitors’ Lions highlighted the role of public engagement in recognising artistic participation.

 

 

 

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed delight over the achievement, describing it as a proud moment for India’s artistic and cultural community. In a post on social media, Prime Minister congratulated the artists and said they are bringing fresh perspectives to the global art world while drawing inspiration from India’s rich and diverse cultural heritage.

United States has proposed fresh tariffs ranging from 15 to 35 per cent on imports from 14 economies, including China, European Union and India. The other economies covered include Taiwan, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Bangladesh and Japan.

 

 

 

 

 

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the proposed measures are aimed at addressing policies that Washington believes disadvantage American manufacturers and weaken the country’s industrial base.

 

 

 

 

 

For India, USTR has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on goods, after accounting for existing Section 301 duties, with exemptions for certain products. It has also proposed considering a 17 per cent rate if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement with the US that addresses the findings of the investigation.

Ministry of Commerce has said that Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement. The Ministry said that the Government has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation concerning Acts, Policies, and Practices of 14 economies, including India, relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors. The Ministry said, the Notice is currently under examination. The Ministry said, India engaged constructively throughout this investigation. It added that in response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.

 

 

 

 

 

The Ministry stated that India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement and it has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations.

Nepal government has begun process to declare 213 Indians missing in August flash floods as presumed dead. The flash floods struck the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system on August 26 this year.

 

 

 

 

 

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) of Nepal has published a list of the 213 missing Indian nationals on its website, inviting objections or requests for corrections in the details provided. More from our correspondent:

         

 

 

 

 

 

 

“The process covers people of all nationalities, including 213 Indian nationals. Nepal’s disaster management authority has published the list of the missing Indians and invited their families to submit any objections or corrections by December 2. The Embassy of India in Kathmandu has urged the families concerned to contact the Embassy through its dedicated email address or WhatsApp helpline to report any objections or changes to the list. After considering their submissions, the Government of Nepal will finalise the list and formally declare the missing persons dead. Arvind Jain, Akashvani News, Kathmandu.”

In Chess, reigning world champion D Gukesh played out a quick 20-move draw with Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva yesterday. Playing with white, Gukesh opted for the London System but failed to gain an advantage as Sindarov comfortably equalised. The Indian agreed to a draw by threefold repetition, with all 30 remaining pieces still on the board. Both players are now level at one point each after two games of the 14-game championship match. The third game will be played today, with Sindarov having the white pieces.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz have reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the India-Germany Strategic Partnership, with a focus on expanding cooperation in defence, advanced technologies, trade and investment. More from our correspondent:-

 

 

“The two leaders held a telephone conversation, during which they reviewed progress in bilateral relations and expressed satisfaction over the sustained momentum in engagements between the two countries. As India and Germany mark 75 years of diplomatic relations this year, both leaders reiterated their commitment to deepening cooperation across key sectors. They also noted that the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement will create new opportunities to expand bilateral trade and investment. During the conversation, PM Modi and Mr Merz exchanged views on regional and global developments of mutual interest. They agreed to work closely to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order. The two leaders also underscored the importance of continued cooperation at multilateral forums to address contemporary global challenges. PAYAL SHARMA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

President Droupadi Murmu has said the younger generation of the country has much to learn from the courage and skills of ancient maritime traders. Addressing Bali Jatra Festival 2026 at Kataka in Odisha, she urged people to draw inspiration from the past to shape the present and build a brighter future. The President said that the Bali Jatra is a unique festival which celebrates the glorious history of Odisha. She said that the merchants from Odisha used to travel to distant lands to engage in trade and commerce. President Murmu said that through trade, they accomplished many significant things for the country. The President noted that the historical connection between Odisha and Bali can be transformed into modern commercial and cultural cooperation.

 

          

On the second day of her Odisha visit, President Droupadi Murmu will attend the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy at Dr. Abhinna Chandra Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital in Bhubaneswar this morning.

Organised at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University, the conference aims to promote higher education, leadership skills, safety and economic self-reliance among women.

During the meeting, the two sides discussed ways to strengthen defence and security cooperation between India and the Maldives.

The sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT) concluded on a high note at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
